segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You then, my child, be strengthened in the grace that is in Christ Jesus,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and what you heard from me in the presence of many witnesses, entrust to faithful people who will be competent to teach others as well.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Take your share of hardship as a good soldier of Christ Jesus.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: No one serving as a soldier gets entangled in the affairs of everyday life, so as to please the one who enlisted him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And if anyone competes as an athlete, he is not crowned unless he competes according to the rules.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: It is the hardworking farmer who ought to have the first share of the crops.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Think over what I am saying, for the Lord will give you understanding in everything.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Remember Jesus Christ, raised from the dead, descended from David, according to my good news,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: for which I am suffering hardship, even to the point of chains, like a criminal. But the word of God is not chained.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For this reason I endure everything for the sake of the chosen, so that they too may obtain the salvation that is in Christ Jesus, with eternal glory.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The saying is trustworthy: For if we died with him, we will also live with him;

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: if we endure, we will also reign with him; if we deny him, he also will deny us;

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: if we are faithless, he remains faithful—he cannot deny himself.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Keep reminding people of these things, solemnly charging them before the Lord not to quarrel about words, which is of no use and only ruins those who listen.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Do your best to present yourself to God as one approved, a worker with nothing to be ashamed of, guiding the word of truth along a straight path.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But keep clear of profane, empty talk, for those who engage in it will advance further into ungodliness,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and their message will spread like gangrene. Among them are Hymenaeus and Philetus,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: who have strayed from the truth, saying that the resurrection has already taken place, and they are overturning the faith of some.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Nevertheless, God’s firm foundation stands, bearing this seal:

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “The Lord knows those who are his,”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and, “Let everyone who names the name of the Lord turn away from wrongdoing.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now in a large house there are not only vessels of gold and silver but also of wood and clay, some for honor and some for dishonor.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So if anyone cleanses themselves from these, that person will be a vessel for honor, made holy, useful to the master, prepared for every good work.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Flee the desires of youth, and pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace, together with those who call on the Lord from a pure heart.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But have nothing to do with foolish and ignorant debates, knowing that they breed quarrels.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And a slave of the Lord must not quarrel but be kind to everyone, able to teach, patient when wronged,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: correcting opponents with gentleness, in the hope that God may grant them a turning back that leads to knowledge of the truth,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and that they may come to their senses and escape the devil’s snare, having been captured alive by him to do his will.

notes.phrase: in the presence of many witnesses
notes.note: The Greek is literally “through many witnesses.” Most interpreters take this as “with many witnesses present,” perhaps recalling Timothy’s commissioning. It could also mean that the teaching reached Timothy by way of many witnesses who confirmed it.

The Greek word was an ordinary term for the public announcement of good news, including imperial proclamations. “Gospel” has become a religious term or a book title, so the plain meaning is given here. Many modern translations alternate between “gospel” and “good news.”

This is the same Greek adjective rendered “faithful” in verses 2 and 13. Said of a statement rather than a person, it means reliable, and “a faithful saying” is no longer natural English. The balanced lines that follow are widely thought to come from an early Christian hymn or confession.

The verb can mean either “not believe” or “be unfaithful.” “Faithless” keeps the deliberate play on “faithful” in the same line and leaves both senses open. Interpreters also differ on whether Christ’s remaining faithful is a comfort (he keeps his promises despite human failure) or a warning (he is true to his word, including the denial just mentioned).

Manuscripts are divided here between “before the Lord” and “before God.” The Greek text followed in this translation reads “the Lord”; several important witnesses and some modern editions read “God.” The sense is little affected.

notes.phrase: guiding the word of truth along a straight path
notes.traditional: rightly dividing the word of truth
notes.note: This rare verb appears in the Greek Old Testament (Proverbs 3:6; 11:5) for making a path straight. Its sense here is debated. Most modern versions give a general “rightly handling” or “correctly handling,” and the older “rightly dividing” presses the idea of cutting. The rendering here follows the Septuagint usage: the message is to be kept on a straight course, not diverted into the word-quarrels of verse 14.

notes.phrase: the resurrection has already taken place
notes.note: The teaching was probably that resurrection is a purely spiritual event already experienced by believers, for example in baptism or conversion, with no future bodily raising to come. The letter gives no further detail, so the exact form of the claim is uncertain.

notes.phrase: “The Lord knows those who are his,”
notes.note: Buildings often carried an inscription or seal marking ownership. The first inscription quotes Numbers 16:5 in the Greek version, from the story of Korah’s rebellion against Moses. The second echoes scriptural language (compare Numbers 16:26; Isaiah 26:13) but is not a direct quotation of any known passage.

“These” may refer to the vessels for dishonor, meaning the false teachers and their company, or more loosely to their teachings and conduct. The Greek leaves it open, and the translation does the same.

The Greek verb is built directly on the ordinary word for “holy,” a link that “sanctified” hides. It means to be brought into the sphere of what belongs to God. Most traditional versions use “sanctified,” while several modern ones use “made holy” or “set apart.”

The Greek word denotes a slave, a person owned by a master, and fits the household image of verses 20–21. “Servant” is the traditional rendering and suggests a hired employee. In the Greek Old Testament “slave of the Lord” is also a title of honor for figures such as Moses and David, which may color the phrase here.

“Meekness” now suggests weakness or timidity, which the Greek word does not. It describes a humble, unassertive manner in dealing with others. “Gentleness” is the usual rendering in modern translations.

“Repentance” now centers on feeling sorry. The Greek word, shaped by the prophets’ call to return to God, means a change of direction in mind and conduct. Most translations keep “repentance” as an established term understood to include a change of life.

notes.phrase: by him to do his will
notes.traditional: taken captive by him at his will
notes.note: The Greek uses two different pronouns for “him” and “his,” and their referents are disputed. The majority view, followed here, is that both refer to the devil. Others read “captured by the devil, but freed to do God’s will,” or “captured alive by the Lord’s slave to do God’s will.”

candidates.reason: Occurs throughout the New Testament and translators split between “slave” and “servant,” both for literal slaves and for the title “slave of the Lord/Christ.”
A core term in every letter where “grace,” “favor” and “gift” are all defensible, so it needs one policy.
Translations vary between “the elect” and “the chosen,” and the former carries later doctrinal weight a reader may import.
Recurs widely and is rendered “lusts,” “passions,” “desires” or “cravings,” which differ markedly in how sexual or negative they sound.
The verb and its noun ὑπομονή recur across the letters and Revelation, with translators varying among “endure,” “persevere,” “patience” and “steadfastness.”

warnings: Verse 21: ἁγιάζω is not rendered with a register form (make holy; consecrate; hold holy / honor as holy; be holy) and has no register-exception note.
